summary: FileWriter and Scanner write and read text files so data lasts after the program ends. try-with-resources makes sure the file is always closed.
notes: new FileWriter("scores.txt") erases the file first. new FileWriter("scores.txt", true) adds to the end.
Values read from a file are Strings, so Integer.parseInt(parts[1]) converts them before adding.
throws IOException on main is required because file methods throw checked exceptions.
pitfall: Without try-with-resources or out.close(), PrintWriter may never write its text to the file, so the file ends up empty.
